items.title: Half of Iran's missile launchers intact after weeks of strikes, assessment finds

featured_image.name: US says it has destroyed Iran missile capacity - Al Jazeera

items.description:
A new U.S. intelligence assessment indicates that roughly half of Iran's missile launchers remain intact and thousands of one-way attack drones are still in its arsenal after five weeks of intensive American and Israeli airstrikes, according to CNN. The findings directly undercut repeated claims by President Trump and senior officials that Iran's military capabilities have been all but eliminated since Operation Epic Fury began on February 28.[1]

In a national address on April 1, Trump told Americans that Iran's "missiles are just about used up or beaten," adding that "their navy is gone, their air force is gone". Earlier, on his Truth Social account, Trump declared that "Iran has been, essentially, decimated". Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has cited a 90 percent drop in Iranian missile launches since the start of the conflict.[2][3]

items.title: US denies Iran's claim it downed warplane near Strait of Hormuz

featured_image.name: US Air Force conducts airstrikes with F-35 for first time ever

items.description:
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps on Thursday claimed it intercepted and destroyed an advanced warplane belonging to the United States and Israel south of Qeshm Island in the Persian Gulf, according to a statement carried by Iranian media. The IRGC said the aircraft crashed into Gulf waters after being struck by its air defense systems, though no details were provided about the type of aircraft or its crew. Iranian state television broadcast footage it said showed the moment the warplane was hit.[1]

US Central Command swiftly rejected the claim. "All U.S. fighter aircraft are accounted for. Iran's IRGC has made the same false claim at least half a dozen times," CENTCOM said in a post on X.[2][3]

items.title: SpaceX in talks with Saudi fund for $5B anchor stake in record IPO

featured_image.name: SpaceX filed confidential SEC IPO papers, eyes $1.75 ...

items.description:
SpaceX has held discussions with Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund about a roughly $5 billion anchor investment in what is shaping up to be the largest initial public offering in history, Reuters reported on Wednesday. The talks come just one day after the rocket and satellite company confidentially filed its IPO registration with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, according to Bloomberg.[1][2][3]

The investment would partly prevent dilution of PIF's existing stake of just under 1% in SpaceX, according to people familiar with the matter. No final decision has been made, and any investment remains subject to change, the sources cautioned.[4][2][1]

items.title: IRGC launches fresh strikes on steel, aluminum plants across Middle East

featured_image.name: Iranian attacks across Gulf continue as major industrial ...

items.description:
Iranian missile and drone strikes have knocked two of the Middle East's largest aluminum smelters offline, pushing prices on the London Metal Exchange to levels not seen since 2022 and raising fears of a prolonged global supply crisis.

The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed responsibility for weekend strikes on March 28 that hit Emirates Global Aluminium's Al Taweelah plant in Abu Dhabi and Aluminium Bahrain's main facility. EGA reported "substantial damage" and injuries to six employees, while Alba said two workers were hurt as it assessed the impact on operations. On April 2, the IRGC announced a fresh "90th wave" of Operation True Promise 4, striking additional steel and aluminum facilities across the region tied to U.S. interests.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Bahrain pushes for Friday UN vote to authorize force in Strait of Hormuz

featured_image.name: Bahrain pushes UN-backed action for Hormuz shipping

items.description:
Bahrain's Foreign Minister Abdullatif bin Rashid Al Zayani on Thursday urged the United Nations Security Council to take a "decisive response" to Iran's effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz, calling for a vote on a Bahraini draft resolution as early as Friday that would authorize "all necessary means" to protect commercial shipping through the critical waterway.[1][2]

Speaking during a high-level Council session that Bahrain chaired as part of its April presidency, Al Zayani condemned Iran's "unlawful and unjustified attempt to control international navigation in the Strait of Hormuz," warning that Tehran's actions threaten energy security, food supplies, and global trade. He also denounced Iranian ballistic missile and drone strikes on Gulf states targeting civilian infrastructure, including airports, water facilities, seaports, and hotels.[3][2][1]

items.title: Trump tells NATO allies to 'get guts' as 40 nations seek to reopen Hormuz

featured_image.name: Is Trump Pulling the U.S. Out of NATO Over Iran War Fallout? - TIME

items.description: President Donald Trump escalated his attacks on NATO on Thursday, urging allied nations to send warships to the Strait of Hormuz and dismissing the alliance as irrelevant, even as more than 40 countries gathered for a UK-led diplomatic summit aimed at reopening the vital waterway without American involvement.

items.title: GCC chief condemns Iran strikes in first-ever UN Council address

featured_image.name: GCC chief urges UN to halt Iranian attacks, protect Gulf waterways

items.description:
In an unprecedented address to the United Nations Security Council on Thursday, Gulf Cooperation Council Secretary-General Jassim Albudaiwi condemned Iran's wave of missile and drone attacks across the Gulf region, warning that the international community stands "at a crossroads" between collective security and the "rule of force."[1][2]

The briefing — the first ever delivered by a GCC secretary-general to the Security Council — came as Bahrain assumed the rotating Council presidency for April and sought to spotlight the growing partnership between the UN and the six-nation Gulf bloc.[3][4]

items.title: US destroys major Iranian bridge as war widens across Gulf

featured_image.name: Key Iranian Bridge Severed By Airstrikes

items.description:
U.S. forces struck the B1 Bridge connecting Tehran to the nearby city of Karaj in two waves of airstrikes on Thursday, severing one of Iran's most prominent infrastructure links as the war entered its 33rd day with no ceasefire in sight. The strike killed eight people and wounded 95 others, according to Ghodratollah Seif, deputy governor of Alborz province, as reported by Fars news agency and Iranian state television.[1][2]

The B1 Bridge, described as one of the tallest highway structures in the Middle East, was hit in two attacks separated by roughly an hour, Iranian state TV reported. A U.S. military official said American forces targeted the bridge because it had been designated as a logistical route for Iran's ballistic missile and drone units, according to The New York Times. The Israeli military said it played no role in the strike. Seif told state media the bridge was not yet operational and that the victims were residents of a nearby village celebrating Nowruz, the Persian New Year.[3][2]

items.title: IRGC claims new strikes on Amazon data center in Bahrain

featured_image.name: IRGC hits Amazon cloud facility in Bahrain

items.description: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps carried out fresh strikes on Amazon Web Services infrastructure in Bahrain this week, marking the latest escalation in a campaign that has repeatedly targeted the cloud giant's Middle Eastern operations since the US-Iran war began in late February.

items.title: SpaceX holds talks with Saudi fund for $5B stake in record IPO

featured_image.name: SpaceX confidentially files for IPO, setting stage for record offering

items.description:
Elon Musk's SpaceX is barreling toward the largest initial public offering in history after confidentially filing registration documents with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission this week and holding talks with Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund about a potential $5 billion cornerstone investment, according to Reuters.[1]

The confidential filing, first reported by Bloomberg on April 1, puts SpaceX on track for a June listing that could value the combined rocket, satellite, and artificial intelligence company at more than $1.75 trillion and raise as much as $75 billion. If completed at that scale, the offering would dwarf Saudi Aramco's $25.6 billion debut in 2019 as the largest IPO on record.[2][3][4][5]

items.title: 40 nations meet on Hormuz crisis as US refuses to join

featured_image.name: UK foreign minister stresses 'urgent need' to reopen Hormuz strait

items.description:
Foreign ministers and representatives from more than 40 countries convened a virtual emergency meeting on Thursday to address the crisis in the Strait of Hormuz, where Iran's blockade has brought one of the world's most vital shipping lanes to a near-standstill since the US-Israeli war against Iran began on February 28. The United States did not take part.[1]

UK Foreign Secretary Yvette Cooper, who chaired the meeting from London, accused Iran of using the waterway as leverage against the global economy. "We have seen Iran hijack an international shipping route to hold the global economy hostage," Cooper said in opening remarks broadcast before the session moved behind closed doors. She said the talks would focus on "collective mobilisation of our full range of diplomatic and economic tools and pressures" to restore freedom of navigation.[1]

items.title: Blue Owl caps fund redemptions after $5.4B in withdrawal requests

featured_image.name: Blue Owl private credit funds redemptions capped at 5% after steep ...

items.description: Blue Owl Capital disclosed on Thursday that it will limit redemptions to 5% at two of its private credit funds after investors sought to pull an unprecedented share of their money during the first quarter, marking the most severe test yet of the embattled private credit sector's ability to manage a wave of investor exits.

items.title: UK hosts 35-nation summit on reopening Strait of Hormuz

featured_image.name: Rookie diplomat Yvette Cooper could not be picking up the Foreign Secretary  reins at a more challenging time | UK News | Sky News

items.description:
Representatives from 35 countries are set to meet Thursday in a virtual summit hosted by the United Kingdom to discuss strategies for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, the critical maritime chokepoint that has been effectively shut down since the U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran began in late February.[1][2]

British Prime Minister Keir Starmer announced the initiative on Wednesday from Downing Street, saying Foreign Secretary Yvette Cooper would chair the session. The meeting will "assess all viable diplomatic and political measures that we can take to restore freedom of navigation, guarantee the safety of trapped ships and seafarers and resume the movement of vital commodities," Starmer said. The United States will not participate in the talks.[3][2][4]

items.title: European stocks drop as Trump vows more strikes on Iran

featured_image.name: European stocks post worst month since 2022 as Iran war drags on

items.description: European markets opened sharply lower on Thursday as investors reacted to President Donald Trump's prime-time address the night before, in which he pledged to escalate military operations against Iran over the coming weeks, dashing hopes that the five-week-old conflict was nearing a swift resolution.

items.title: Magnitude 7.4 earthquake kills one in Indonesia, triggers brief tsunami warning

featured_image.name: Magnitude 7.4 earthquake off Indonesia topples buildings ...

items.description: A powerful undersea earthquake struck Indonesia's Molucca Sea early Thursday, toppling buildings across parts of northern Indonesia, killing at least one person, and generating small tsunami waves before warnings were lifted hours later.

items.title: Iraq's oil exports halt as Hormuz closure cuts output 70%

featured_image.name: Iraq's Oil Output Plunges 70% as Gulf Shipping Crisis Deepens

items.description:
More than a month into the war between the United States, Israel, and Iran, Iraq's oil industry — the backbone of its economy — has been brought to its knees. Oil production across the southern province of Basra has plunged by more than 70 percent, exports from the country's main terminals have been completely halted, and hundreds of foreign workers have fled the country, according to an Associated Press report from Basra published this week.[1]

Output across Basra province has dropped from 3.1 million barrels per day to roughly 900,000, Bassem Abdul Karim, head of the state-run Basra Oil Company, told the AP. "Exports are currently completely halted. At the moment, we are considering alternative loading areas, but none are fully operational," he said.[1]

items.title: Korean researchers achieve lithium-air battery breakthrough

featured_image.name: Korean team's battery breakthrough locks anode materials in ...

items.description: A joint research team from South Korea has developed a novel catalyst that overcomes key performance barriers in lithium-air batteries, a technology long considered the holy grail of energy storage for its potential to deliver up to ten times the energy density of conventional lithium-ion systems.[1]

items.title: NASA's Artemis II crew orbits Earth after historic moonshot launch

featured_image.name: Artemis II Flight Update: Apogee Raise Burn Complete, Crew Looks Ahead to Proximity  Operations - NASA

items.description: NASA's four Artemis II astronauts have reached a stable orbit, clearing the first critical milestone of their journey to the Moon. The crew's Orion capsule successfully separated from the Space Launch System rocket and completed its initial orbital checks, with a trans-lunar injection burn planned for Thursday evening that will send them on their way to the lunar surface.

items.title: Trump says Strait of Hormuz will 'open up naturally,' rattling markets

featured_image.name: Trump declares other countries need to 'take the lead' on the Strait of ...

items.description: President Trump told the nation Wednesday night that the Strait of Hormuz — the narrow waterway through which roughly 20% of the world's oil supply flows — would "open up naturally" once the month-old war with Iran concludes, offering no concrete plan to reopen the critical shipping lane and sending financial markets into a tailspin.[1][2]

items.title: Trump vows to hit Iran 'extremely hard' for weeks

featured_image.name: Trump speech live updates: President addresses the nation on Iran

items.description: President Donald Trump told the nation on Wednesday night that the United States would continue striking Iran "extremely hard" for another two to three weeks, dashing investor hopes for a clearer signal that the month-long conflict was winding down and sending markets into retreat overnight.
